title: reduce streaming token latency: token loop, flush cadence, backpressure, kernel scheduling, kv-cache batching
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: Streaming token latency has been a recurring customer pain point for low-latency chat scenarios. High tail latency is driven by a combination of token-loop scheduling inefficiencies, suboptimal flush cadence under backpressure, and kernel scheduling that does not prioritize small interactive responses. This PR implements a multi-pronged optimization: 1) rewrite of the streaming token loop to reduce allocations and make flush decisions opportunistically; 2) adaptive flush cadence based on observed backpressure and KV-cache hit rates; 3) a small-change kernel scheduler that prefers low-latency kernel paths for interactive requests; 4) tighter integration between continuous batching and KV cache so we emit partial prefixes earlier when safe. The result is a measurable reduction in median and p95 token emission latency across our benchmark suite and improved stability under bursty traffic.
